citation: Wolf, R., Latham, G., Armstrong, C., Ross, S., Laurenzano, M., Daniels, C., Eisinger, J., & Reilly, J. (2018). English Language and Literacy Acquisition-Validation (ELLA-V) i3 Evaluation (Valid 22): Final report. Baltimore, MD: Johns Hopkins University, School of Education, Center for Research and Reform in Education. (ERIC No. ED598313)
report_number: i3 PR/Award U411B120047; ELLA-V Valid 22 Final Report (Aug 2018); ERIC ED598313 (grantee submission) / ED594703
design: Multisite cluster (school-level) RCT, three conditions: Treatment 1 (T1), Treatment 2 (T2), and Business-as-Usual (BAU). 79 schools in 10 Texas districts randomized in triads (mostly 3 schools/block) by the independent evaluator; analytic schools per contrast ~40-46 (T+C). Backwards grade rollout, one grade per year (grade 3 in 2013-14, grade 2 in 2014-15, grade 1 in 2015-16, kindergarten in 2016-17); teachers/students exposed for one school year. Predominantly low-income, majority English-learner (EL) population. Subjects: literacy/oral language/English-language development (Reading), science (STEM), writing (Other). T1 and T2 received equivalent teacher PD and coaching but different curricula; impacts estimated separately for each treatment vs BAU and separately by grade via 2-level HLM (students nested in schools) with grand-mean-centered pretest and school/district covariates; propensity-score weighting added where baseline equivalence failed.
problems: Two registry arms (136, 137) map to Treatment 1 (row 136) and Treatment 2 (row 137), each vs the common Business-as-Usual control. The report does not assign each numeric row_id to a treatment, so the 136->T1 / 137->T2 mapping is inferred (alphabetical/ordinal); if the meta-analysis intended the reverse, swap the two arms' values. Self-esteem outcomes (SEI English/Spanish) are affective, not academic achievement, and were excluded per spec. ICC/design-effect is NOT reported anywhere in the report and was not guessed (icc=null); however the impact estimates and SEs come from multilevel (mixed) models with schools as a level-2 random effect, so cluster_adjusted=true and no further central cluster correction is needed. df were reported as 'infinity' for all models; J was computed from the analytic student N. The report's own 'Std. Effect Size' = impact estimate / unadjusted pooled SD; g was computed the same way with Hedges' J applied (g matches the reported ES to within rounding) and g_se = J*(impact_se/pooled_SD). Extracted here are the report's CONFIRMATORY contrasts (one designated grade per outcome domain per treatment, flagged 'C' in the master contrast list, Tables C1/C2) covering all reported academic-achievement domains: science (STEM), oral language, phonological awareness, reading achievement (STAAR), English-language development in reading (WMLS-R), reading fluency (DIBELS), and writing (Other). Numerous additional EXPLORATORY by-grade contrasts exist for the same instruments/domains (e.g., oral language and ELD in grades 1-3, TELPAS ELD/Reading in all grades) and are not extracted individually to avoid over-weighting; the meta-analysis coded this study as contributing three domains (Reading, STEM, Other) per arm. Notable significant exploratory results not extracted: T1 grade-1 oral language was significantly negative (g~-0.09); T2 grade-1 oral language significantly positive (g~+0.12); both kindergarten oral-language confirmatory contrasts (extracted) were significantly positive.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Treatment 1 (T1: SEI/EIR/CRISELLA science-infused literacy curricula + ELLA-V PD/coaching) vs Business-as-Usual
effect_sizes.test_name: Iowa Test of Basic Skills (ITBS) science subtest
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring Y1, end of one-year treatment; grade 3 = 2013-14)
effect_sizes.g_method: g = J*d, d = impact_estimate(5.63)/pooled_SD(21.06) = 0.267 (matches report Std Effect Size 0.27); pooled SD = unadjusted pooled posttest SD from Table C4; J=0.9994 from analytic N=1317. g_se = J*(impact_se/pooled_SD) = 0.9994*(2.83/21.06).
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 5 (p.25); Table C4 row T1_Students_1_Gr3 (p.56); descriptives Table B1 (p.46)
effect_sizes.notes: Confirmatory contrast (C). Statistically significant positive impact (p=.047): the only significant positive achievement effect among the headline outcomes; T1 grade-3 received the intensive science-infused literacy curriculum (CRISELLA). Standardized/independent norm-referenced test, individually administered by trained testers. mean_t not separately reported (Table 5 gives unadjusted control mean 185.94 only).

effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring Y1, end of one-year treatment; kindergarten = 2016-17)
effect_sizes.g_method: g = J*d, d = 4.15/26.03 = 0.159 (matches report Std Effect Size 0.16); pooled SD 26.03 from Table C4; J=0.9993 (N=1146). g_se = 0.9993*(0.92/26.03).

effect_sizes.notes: Confirmatory contrast (C). Statistically significant positive oral-language impact (p<.001) for kindergarten, where T1 curriculum most emphasized oral language. Reading/literacy domain -> Reading. Low-stakes individually administered language test.
